children: RideNow’s third-quarter revenue fell 13.1% year over year, while its net loss widened, reflecting lower retail vehicle sales amid cautious consumer spending and the initial impact of its Clear Price model. Six fewer stores and the wind-down of transportation services also weighed on revenue; lower compensation and facilities costs partly offset the decline.
¹ Reported as “Total revenue”. ² Reported as “Net loss”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.
: Total powersports unit sales fell 19.2% to 12,886; retail unit sales declined 16.6% to 12,182.
: Revenue decreased 7.9% to $241.4M, and gross profit declined 8.6% to $65.8M.
: The all-in pricing model launched across the dealership group in the third quarter; management cited short-term competitive price disparities and lower retail traffic.
: RideNow operated 46 dealerships as of September 30, 2026, primarily in the Sunbelt region.
: The company acquired a powersports retailer in Tallahassee, Florida, for $4.1M during the quarter.
